description: The Wide Field Instrument is Roman's primary camera and slitless spectrometer. It has eight imaging filters spanning 0.48 to 2.3 microns, plus a grism and a prism, and NASA publishes the wavelength edges and effective-area tables as technical information.
facility_description: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is a NASA mission whose primary science instrument is the Wide Field Instrument.
notes: The WFI page links Schlieder et al. 2024 at https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024SPIE13092E..0SS/abstract and says the subsystem figure is adapted from that paper. The paper itself was not opened, so it is a top-level reference only and is not used as a passband citation. https://roman.gsfc.nasa.gov/ returns HTTP 200 but is only a meta refresh to https://science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/roman-for-scientists/, so the live NASA Science pages are linked instead. No journal paper that publishes these passbands was opened: ADS and SciX returned a verification challenge or an empty body, and the Schlieder et al. 2024 SPIE link on the WFI page (bibcode in the URL 2024SPIE13092E..0SS) was not opened as a paper, so there is no references key and no bands.*.references. The machine-readable filter table opened this session gives wavelength_min and wavelength_max in microns: F062 0.48-0.76, F087 0.76-0.977, F106 0.927-1.192, F129 1.131-1.454, F158 1.380-1.774, F184 1.683-2.000, F213 1.95-2.30, F146 0.927-2.000. The STScI observatory table gives slightly rounder ranges (for example F087 0.76-0.98 and F158 1.38-1.77) and labels the elements F062 (R) through F213 (Ks). Those table cells are not copied into per-band Description fields because they are not sentences. The same NASA page's grism/prism parameter table names the elements G150 and P127, with resolving power 461 times wavelength in microns for the grism and 80-180 (2 pix) for the prism; the prose on that page says the grism resolution is ~600 and the prism resolution is ~100, while the STScI page says R=460*λ (μm) and R=80-180. The MAST acknowledgement is the text MAST asks authors to use for Roman observations. It contains fill-in brackets and says the data were obtained from MAST; the filter tables cited here are on NASA Science and the Roman technical-information repository, not identified on those pages as MAST products. Two spaces after 'Roman.' follow the HTML, which has a non-breaking space and then a normal space. STScI's content-use page says material it produced may be freely used as in the public domain and requests acknowledgement of NASA and STScI, but it does not give a fixed sentence beyond that request. No photon-versus-energy counting statement for WFI photometry was found on the pages opened.

Grism.Description: WFI slitless grism with a bandpass spanning 1.0 to 1.93 microns.
Grism.Comments: Mean over the 18 SCAs of the Grism_1stOrder column of the Roman technical-information effective-area tables (Roman_effarea_v8_SCA01..18_20240301.ecsv; CC0), divided by the 4.374354 m^2 area of the 2.36 m aperture stop, so values are a throughput relative to that area (central obscuration not removed). Pivot 14225.0 Å. It replaced the earlier SVO-copied curve on 2026-10-26; that curve is kept as Grism_old. Per-detector curves: Roman/WFI_SCA01..WFI_SCA18.
